QF.id: Introduction to AML, CFT and Proliferation Financing_4

question.text: In the context of money laundering, "smurfing" refers to:

answer.text: Using shell companies to hide beneficial ownership
Breaking large amounts of money into smaller sums deposited below the AML reporting threshold
Creating fake employee payrolls to extract laundered money

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines smurfing as a placement-stage technique in which small amounts of money, each kept below the AML reporting threshold, are inserted into bank accounts or credit cards. The objective is to avoid triggering single-transaction reporting limits. The Trap: Shell-company use (option A) and cross-border cash smuggling (option B) are other placement methods, but the workbook does not label them "smurfing". Fake-employee payrolls (option D) is an integration technique used to extract laundered money rather than a placement technique. Note: The PML Rules also require reporting of connected cash transactions whose daily/monthly aggregate crosses the prescribed threshold, so smurfed deposits can still trigger reporting once aggregated.
